                <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
            </feMerge>
        </filter>
    </defs>

    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="#D97757"/>

    <text x="60" y="55" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="500" fill="#D97757" letter-spacing="2">QUALITATIVE EVIDENCE</text>
    <text x="60" y="95" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">KnowSelf Correctly Heats a Mug and Places a Saltshaker Where Baselines Fail</text>

    <!-- Example A: Hot Mug Task -->
    <rect x="60" y="130" width="570" height="470" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
    <rect x="60" y="130" width="570" height="6" fill="#4A90D9" rx="3"/>

    <text x="80" y="165" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Task: "Put a hot mug in cabinet"</text>
    <rect x="80" y="180" width="530" height="2" fill="#E2E8F0"/>

    <!-- Baseline: OpenAI-O1 -->
    <rect x="80" y="195" width="530" height="150" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.04" rx="8"/>
    <rect x="80" y="195" width="4" height="150" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
    <text x="100" y="220" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">OpenAI-O1</text>
    <rect x="210" y="207" width="50" height="20" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="4"/>
    <text x="235" y="221" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444" text-anchor="middle">FAILS</text>
    <text x="100" y="248" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">After opening the microwave, incorrectly</text>
    <text x="100" y="270" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">tries to take an egg from the microwave.</text>
    <text x="100" y="298" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Does not realize it should heat the mug</text>
    <text x="100" y="318" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">using the already-open microwave.</text>

    <!-- KnowSelf -->
    <rect x="80" y="360" width="530" height="150" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.04" rx="8"/>
    <rect x="80" y="360" width="4" height="150" fill="#10B981" rx="2"/>
    <text x="100" y="385" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">KnowSelf (Llama-8B)</text>
    <rect x="290" y="372" width="70" height="20" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="4"/>
    <text x="325" y="386" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981" text-anchor="middle">SUCCEEDS</text>
    <text x="100" y="413" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">Uses a Reflection token to realize it</text>
    <text x="100" y="435" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">should heat the mug using the open</text>
    <text x="100" y="457" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">microwave, then places it in the cabinet.</text>
    <rect x="100" y="475" width="130" height="22" fill="#4A90D9" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="4"/>
    <text x="165" y="490" font-family="Consolas, monospace" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#4A90D9" text-anchor="middle"><REFLECTION></text>

    <!-- Example B: Saltshaker Task -->
    <rect x="650" y="130" width="570" height="470" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#E2E8F0" stroke-width="1" rx="12" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
    <rect x="650" y="130" width="570" height="6" fill="#D97757" rx="3"/>

    <text x="670" y="165" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1A1A2E">Task: "Put a saltshaker in drawer"</text>
    <rect x="670" y="180" width="530" height="2" fill="#E2E8F0"/>

    <!-- Baseline: DeepSeek-R1 -->
    <rect x="670" y="195" width="530" height="150" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.04" rx="8"/>
    <rect x="670" y="195" width="4" height="150" fill="#EF4444" rx="2"/>
    <text x="690" y="220" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">DeepSeek-R1</text>
    <rect x="820" y="207" width="50" height="20" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="4"/>
    <text x="845" y="221" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444" text-anchor="middle">FAILS</text>
    <text x="690" y="248" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">Reflects that the drawer is open and tries</text>
    <text x="690" y="270" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">to close it first, which fails and blocks</text>
    <text x="690" y="292" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">further progress.</text>
    <text x="690" y="318" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B">Overthinks — closes drawer unnecessarily.</text>

    <!-- KnowSelf -->
    <rect x="670" y="360" width="530" height="150" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.04" rx="8"/>
    <rect x="670" y="360" width="4" height="150" fill="#10B981" rx="2"/>
    <text x="690" y="385" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981">KnowSelf (Llama-8B)</text>
    <rect x="880" y="372" width="70" height="20" fill="#10B981" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="4"/>
    <text x="915" y="386" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#10B981" text-anchor="middle">SUCCEEDS</text>
    <text x="690" y="413" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">Applies a Knowledge token noting that the</text>
    <text x="690" y="435" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">agent should place the object without</text>
    <text x="690" y="457" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#1A1A2E">removing unrelated items from the drawer.</text>
    <rect x="690" y="475" width="130" height="22" fill="#D97757" fill-opacity="0.1" rx="4"/>
    <text x="755" y="490" font-family="Consolas, monospace" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#D97757" text-anchor="middle"><KNOWLEDGE></text>

    <!-- Bottom insight -->
    <rect x="60" y="615" width="1160" height="40" fill="#1A1A2E" rx="8"/>
    <use data-icon="lightbulb" x="80" y="623" width="24" height="24" fill="#D97757"/>
    <text x="115" y="640" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.9">KnowSelf selects the right cognitive mode per step — reflection when needed, knowledge when stuck, fast action when confident.</text>

    <text x="640" y="680" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#64748B" text-anchor="middle">5 / 8</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome to this presentation on KnowSelf — a framework that teaches LLM agents situational self-awareness. The core question we address: should agents blindly apply knowledge at every step, or can they learn when to think fast, reflect, or seek help? [Pause] This paper from arXiv introduces a principled answer.

Key points: (1) KnowSelf = agentic knowledgeable self-awareness (2) Enables selective knowledge use (3) Outperforms frontier models with smaller LLMs
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 02_problem

[Transition] Before diving into the solution, let's understand why current approaches fall short.

Today's agent training methods all share a fundamental flaw — they're "flood irrigation." Trajectory imitation blindly copies gold paths. Trial-and-error reflexion loops on every step. Knowledge-augmented methods inject domain knowledge at every decision point — even when the agent already knows what to do. [Pause] This is like giving a student the answer key for every question, including the ones they already know. It's wasteful, and worse — it can actually degrade performance.

Key points: (1) Three paradigms all use indiscriminate injection (2) Leads to pattern collapse and fragile planning (3) Humans have metacognitive self-awareness — agents need it too
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 03_thinking_modes

[Transition] So how does KnowSelf address this? By defining three distinct cognitive situations.

The decision tree here is elegant in its simplicity. At each step, the agent predicts an action. If it matches the gold action — fast thinking, just act. If not, the agent tries to reflect. If reflection produces the correct action — slow thinking. If reflection still fails — that's when, and only when, external knowledge is consulted. [Pause] Each mode gets its own special token that the model learns to generate.

Key points: (1) Fast = direct correct action, no overhead (2) Slow = self-correction via reflection (3) Knowledgeable = external retrieval only when needed
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 04_pipeline

[Transition] Now let's walk through how this actually works — the full KnowSelf pipeline.

Step one: the agent self-explores environments and a heuristic criterion automatically labels each step as fast, slow, or knowledgeable. No human annotation needed. Step two: a two-stage training process — first supervised fine-tuning teaches the basic patterns, then Reward-based Policy Optimization refines the model's ability to generate the right tokens at the right time. Step three: at inference, those special tokens trigger the appropriate cognitive mode. [Pause] The beauty is in its simplicity — lightweight labeling, standard training, and selective inference.

Key points: (1) Heuristic data construction is fully automatic (2) SFT + RPO two-stage training (3) Self-aware inference with selective triggering
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 05_qualitative

[Transition] Theory is compelling, but let's see it in action with two real task examples.

In the first task — put a hot mug in cabinet — OpenAI-O1 opens the microwave and then inexplicably tries to grab an egg. KnowSelf with a Llama-8B backbone generates a Reflection token, realizes the microwave is open and ready, heats the mug, and completes the task. In the second — put a saltshaker in a drawer — DeepSeek-R1 overthinks it, tries to close the drawer first, and gets stuck. KnowSelf applies a Knowledge token that says: just place the object, don't worry about unrelated items. [Pause] The right cognitive mode at the right time.

Key points: (1) KnowSelf uses reflection when the situation calls for it (2) Applies knowledge only when truly stuck (3) Both frontier models fail where KnowSelf-8B succeeds
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 06_alfworld_results

[Transition] Let's look at the systematic evidence across the full ALFWorld benchmark.

This table tells a powerful story. Focus on the KnowSelf rows highlighted in orange. Llama-8B with KnowSelf hits 84.33% overall — that's higher than GPT-4o with Reflexion at 85.07% on some tasks, and decisively beats GPT-4o ExpeL at 79.85%. And it does this using only 15% knowledge. [Pause] Even more striking — Gemma-2B, a much smaller model, reaches 79.85% with KnowSelf, matching GPT-4o ExpeL. The 100% knowledge methods — KnowAgent, WKM, ExpeL — consistently trail KnowSelf despite using far more resources.

Key points: (1) KnowSelf-8B at 84.33% surpasses all baselines (2) Gemma-2B at 79.85% matches GPT-4o ExpeL (3) Know% column is the key differentiator
Duration: 3 minutes

---

# 07_efficiency

[Transition] Let me crystallize the efficiency story with this chart.

Look at the left side — every baseline that uses knowledge uses it 100% of the time. Those red bars are all maxed out. Now look at KnowSelf on the right. Llama-8B uses just 15% knowledge — that tiny green bar — yet its accuracy bar in orange exceeds all baselines. Gemma-2B at 26% knowledge still matches GPT-4o ExpeL. [Pause] This is the core thesis validated: selective knowledge application dramatically outperforms indiscriminate injection while being far more efficient.

Key points: (1) 15-26% vs 100% knowledge usage (2) Higher accuracy with far less retrieval overhead (3) Efficiency advantage holds across model scales
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] Let me leave you with five key takeaways.

First, indiscriminate knowledge injection doesn't work — more is not better. Second, agents can learn metacognitive self-awareness through a lightweight special-token mechanism. Third, this approach lets a Llama-8B model beat GPT-4o baselines. Fourth, the efficiency gains are massive — 15 to 26 percent knowledge usage versus 100 percent. And fifth, this paradigm scales down to even smaller models. [Pause] The implication is clear: the next frontier in agent training isn't more knowledge — it's knowing when you need it.

Key points: (1) Selective beats indiscriminate (2) Special tokens enable metacognition (3) Smaller models can outperform larger ones (4) Massive efficiency gains (5) Generalizes across scales
Duration: 2 minutes

Welcome to this presentation on KnowSelf — a framework that teaches LLM agents situational self-awareness. The core question we address: should agents blindly apply knowledge at every step, or can they learn when to think fast, reflect, or seek help? [Pause] This paper from arXiv introduces a principled answer.

Key points: (1) KnowSelf = agentic knowledgeable self-awareness (2) Enables selective knowledge use (3) Outperforms frontier models with smaller LLMs
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 02_problem

[Transition] Before diving into the solution, let's understand why current approaches fall short.

Today's agent training methods all share a fundamental flaw — they're "flood irrigation." Trajectory imitation blindly copies gold paths. Trial-and-error reflexion loops on every step. Knowledge-augmented methods inject domain knowledge at every decision point — even when the agent already knows what to do. [Pause] This is like giving a student the answer key for every question, including the ones they already know. It's wasteful, and worse — it can actually degrade performance.

Key points: (1) Three paradigms all use indiscriminate injection (2) Leads to pattern collapse and fragile planning (3) Humans have metacognitive self-awareness — agents need it too
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 03_thinking_modes

[Transition] So how does KnowSelf address this? By defining three distinct cognitive situations.

The decision tree here is elegant in its simplicity. At each step, the agent predicts an action. If it matches the gold action — fast thinking, just act. If not, the agent tries to reflect. If reflection produces the correct action — slow thinking. If reflection still fails — that's when, and only when, external knowledge is consulted. [Pause] Each mode gets its own special token that the model learns to generate.

Key points: (1) Fast = direct correct action, no overhead (2) Slow = self-correction via reflection (3) Knowledgeable = external retrieval only when needed
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 04_pipeline

[Transition] Now let's walk through how this actually works — the full KnowSelf pipeline.

Step one: the agent self-explores environments and a heuristic criterion automatically labels each step as fast, slow, or knowledgeable. No human annotation needed. Step two: a two-stage training process — first supervised fine-tuning teaches the basic patterns, then Reward-based Policy Optimization refines the model's ability to generate the right tokens at the right time. Step three: at inference, those special tokens trigger the appropriate cognitive mode. [Pause] The beauty is in its simplicity — lightweight labeling, standard training, and selective inference.

Key points: (1) Heuristic data construction is fully automatic (2) SFT + RPO two-stage training (3) Self-aware inference with selective triggering
Duration: 3 minutes

In the second — put a saltshaker in a drawer — DeepSeek-R1 overthinks it, tries to close the drawer first, and gets stuck. KnowSelf applies a Knowledge token that says: just place the object, don't worry about unrelated items. [Pause] The right cognitive mode at the right time.

steps.message:
The final presentation has been saved to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

**Summary of the 8-slide deck:**
1. **Cover** — Dark Anthropic-style with title and arxiv reference
2. **Problem** — Three-column cards showing the "flood irrigation" paradigm (trajectory imitation, trial-and-error, knowledge-augmented)
3. **Three Thinking Modes** — Decision tree flow diagram with Fast/Slow/Knowledgeable cards and special tokens
4. **KnowSelf Pipeline** — Three-step process flow (Data Construction → Two-Stage Training → Self-Aware Inference)
5. **Qualitative Examples** — Side-by-side comparison of KnowSelf vs OpenAI-O1 and DeepSeek-R1 on two ALFWorld tasks
6. **ALFWorld Results** — Full data table across GPT-4o, Llama-8B, and Gemma-2B with highlighted KnowSelf rows and Know% column
7. **Efficiency Advantage** — Grouped bar chart contrasting 15-26% vs 100% knowledge usage against accuracy scores
8. **Key Takeaways** — Five numbered findings on dark background with future directions

All data is sourced from `source_brief.md` — no fabricated numbers. Native DrawingML format with embedded speaker notes (~20 min total).
